name: DropdownMenu

knownIssues.summary: Alignment is physical (`left` | `right`) where Table and Form use logical `start` | `end` (shared-value-names).

purpose: Pairs any trigger element with a floating Menu panel.
intent: A thin composition of Popup (positioning/dismissal) and Menu (search/sectioning/selection/keyboard nav) preconfigured for the click-to-open action-menu use case, rather than a third independent implementation of either concern.

sourceFiles.note: No dropdown-menu.module.css - the component has no visual styling of its own; every visible pixel comes from Popup's panel skin (padding="none") and Menu's own row/section styles.

figmaSource.structure: Variants cross `trigger` (avatar/icon-button/button/link-button/chip-base/chip-operator/chip-value/tag/page-selector - 9 distinct trigger types, default avatar) x `alignment` (left/center/right, default left) x `isOpen` (true/false, not fully crossed with alignment). Every variant instantiates the same `popup` component (the exact component set Popup wraps) with a `trigger` SLOT holding the trigger instance, and a `surface` SLOT holding `figma-parts / panelSurface` (Popup's own skin) whose own `content` SLOT holds a `menu` instance. The measured padding around that nested menu instance is 0 on every axis.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 9-value `trigger` variant became a generic `children: React.ReactElement` prop, not a variant enum - matching Popup's own `children` model ("the single trigger element") rather than hardcoding a closed set of trigger shapes. Any focusable element works; the 9 Figma values are demonstrated in Storybook's Content story as examples, not enforced as an allowed list.

Figma's `alignment` (left/center/right) maps to Popup's `bottomLeft`/`bottomCenter`/`bottomRight` specifically - Dropdown Menu always opens below its trigger, matching the fact that Figma's dropdown-menu has no top/bottom axis at all. Popup's own viewport-fit fallback (trying the top* counterpart, then the remaining alignments) still applies underneath when there's no room below - a capability Figma doesn't model, inherited for free rather than re-derived.
`isOpen` became the existing `open`/`onOpenChange` controlled pair (Popup's own prop names), not a new prop - same native-attribute-first reasoning as Popup's own isOpen->open adaptation.

The measured zero padding around the nested `menu` instance is what motivated adding a fourth value, `'none'`, to Popup's own `padding` prop (see popup.contract.json apiAdaptationNotes, dated 2026-08-19) rather than having Dropdown Menu set `unstyled` and re-declare background/border/radius/shadow itself.

DropdownMenuProps extends MenuProps (minus id/className, which apply to Popup's panel instead) rather than accepting an opaque `content: React.ReactNode` the way Popup does - every real Figma instance of dropdown-menu nests a `menu` instance specifically, never arbitrary content, so the code API guides toward that same shape directly instead of requiring the consumer to manually construct a <Menu> every time.

useCases: A click-to-open action menu anchored to a button, icon button, avatar, tag, chip, or other trigger
antiPatterns: A non-interactive hover hint - use Tooltip
Floating content that isn't a list of actions/options - use Popup directly with your own content

anatomy.name: trigger
anatomy.description: The single child element (children) - any focusable control. Cloned by DropdownMenu to receive a ref (for returning focus) and aria-haspopup="menu" (unless it sets its own), then by the underlying Popup to receive a measurement ref and aria-expanded/aria-controls.

anatomy.name: panel
anatomy.description: Popup's own default visual skin (background/border/radius/shadow), rendered with padding="none".

anatomy.name: menu
anatomy.description: A Menu, rendered with every Menu prop DropdownMenu accepts (an explicit list; fullWidth is also set by matchTriggerWidth), with each item's onSelect wrapped to close the panel.

onOpenChange.description: Called with false on Escape or an outside click.

alignment.description: Maps to Popup's bottomLeft/bottomCenter/bottomRight - always opens below the trigger.

anchorRef.description: Element to measure for positioning and width instead of the trigger child - forwarded to Popup. Use when the ARIA-bearing trigger is smaller than the visual control (e.g. Select's inset input within its field frame).

matchTriggerWidth.description: Sizes the panel to the trigger (or anchorRef) and passes fullWidth to the inner Menu so it fills that width - so a field's dropdown matches the field's width. Forwarded to Popup.

id.description: Applied to Popup's floating panel, not to Menu's root.

className.description: Composes with Popup's panel class list, not with Menu's root.

sections.description: Forwarded to Menu unchanged - see menu.contract.json.

left.purpose: Opens below the trigger, left edges aligned - matches Figma's default.

center.purpose: Opens below the trigger, horizontally centered.

right.purpose: Opens below the trigger, right edges aligned.

triggeredBy: consumer-controlled - same as Popup; Dropdown Menu attaches no open handler, and reports closing through onOpenChange(false)
accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the trigger by Popup, reflecting open
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the trigger by Popup, pointing at the panel id while open
accessibility.role: menu (set by the inner Menu, not by DropdownMenu/Popup directly)
accessibility.ariaHaspopup: menu, set on the trigger by DropdownMenu unless the trigger sets its own
accessibility.focusManagement: menu-button pattern: opening moves focus to the search field or the first enabled row (one animation frame later, once Popup has made the panel visible); choosing an item, Escape, or Tab/Shift+Tab out of the panel returns focus to the trigger. Skipped for a role="combobox" trigger (Select), which keeps focus.

behaviorRules: open is a required, fully controlled prop, inherited from Popup - no internal open state, no defaultOpen.
Always renders a Menu as Popup's content - there is no way to pass arbitrary non-Menu content (use Popup directly for that).
alignment only ever resolves to a bottom* Popup alignment as the preference - Popup's own top*/opposite-side fallback still applies if that overflows the viewport.

Choosing an item runs its onSelect, then returns focus to the trigger and calls onOpenChange(false) - unless that onSelect called event.preventDefault(), which keeps the panel open (e.g. a checkbox row). Not applied for a role="combobox" trigger.
Tab past the panel's last tab stop, or Shift+Tab before its first, calls onOpenChange(false) and returns focus to the trigger.
Renders nothing but the trigger when open is false, identical to Popup.
compositionRules: Pass Menu's own props (sections, showSearch, etc.) directly to DropdownMenu - do not construct a separate <Menu> and try to pass it as content.
Call event.preventDefault() in an item's onSelect when choosing it should keep the dropdown open.
responsiveRules: Inherits Popup's resize/scroll-driven repositioning identically across breakpoints.

Storybook-preview caveat, not a component defect: scrolling Storybook's OUTER docs/canvas page (rather than the story iframe's own content) will not reposition an open panel, because `position: fixed` is fixed to the iframe's own viewport - that iframe's `window` never receives a scroll event for the outer page's scroll, so Popup's listener (correctly implemented - verified directly by dispatching a scroll event and observing it recalculate) has no signal to respond to. Affects Tooltip/Inline Message identically, since all three share Popup's mechanism. Does not occur in the real app, which isn't iframe-embedded.
themeRules: Inherits Popup's and Menu's token-driven theming - no component-level light/dark branching of its own.

tokens.note: DropdownMenu introduces no tokens of its own - every visible value comes from Popup (background/border/radius/shadow) and Menu (row/section/selection colors, spacing, typography, per-size width). See popup.contract.json and menu.contract.json.

do: Pass Menu's own props directly to DropdownMenu rather than constructing a separate Menu element.
Let choosing an item close the dropdown; call event.preventDefault() in onSelect only to keep it open.
dont: Do not expect a content prop for non-Menu floating content - use Popup directly instead.
Do not wrap the trigger in another element - the wrapper, not the button, gets the ARIA and the returned focus.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders only the trigger when open is false; renders the trigger plus a role="menu" panel when open is true.
Sets aria-expanded/aria-controls on the trigger, reflecting open (inherited from Popup).
Maps alignment left/center/right to Popup's bottomLeft/bottomCenter/bottomRight exactly, defaulting to left.
Calls onOpenChange(false) on Escape and on an outside click by default (inherited from Popup), on Tab out of the panel, and after a chosen item's onSelect unless it called event.preventDefault().
Sets aria-haspopup="menu" on the trigger unless it sets its own.
Moves focus into the panel on open (search field, else first enabled row) and returns it to the trigger on choose, Escape, and Tab out.

Forwards every Menu prop (sections, size, showSearch, searchValue/onSearchChange, searchPlaceholder, searchLabel, clearSearchLabel, showScrollbar, maxHeight, loading, loadingLabel, emptyMessage, fullWidth, aria-label, aria-labelledby) to the rendered Menu; sections with each onSelect wrapped.
Renders the panel with Popup's default visual skin and padding="none", so Menu sits flush against it.
Supports a custom id/className on the panel (Popup's, not Menu's root).
knownLimitations: No support for non-Menu panel content - a consumer needing that composes Popup directly instead.
Inherits every one of Menu's own knownLimitations (no custom scrollbar widget, no typeahead).
futureEnhancements: Arrow Down/Up on the trigger to open the menu on its first/last row (the full menu-button keyboard model).
